turns.doctor_question: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because... well, I keep hearing people talking about me. It's usually through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's the board members, mostly, or my staff. They're always saying I'm ruining the company. And it sounds so incredibly clear that I actually answer them back before I realize no one else in the room heard a thing. It's just like that time we were redesigning the lobby. I told the interior decorator—this woman named Sheila, she had the most atrocious taste in floral arrangements, just absolutely garish—I told her that the marble needed to be imported from Italy, not that cheap domestic stuff she was pushing. You know, you really have to watch people in that industry, they'll cut corners anywhere they can just to save a dime, and then who looks bad? I do. The CEO always takes the fall. Just like how they're trying to make me take the fall now with all this whispering.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient reports hearing clear voices of board members and staff talking about them through walls and turned-off phones when no one else hears them.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality and derailment, shifting from discussing hallucinations to an unrelated story about an interior decorator, floral arrangements, and Italian marble.

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I sleep fine when I can actually get to sleep, but it's hard when you have a company to run. You know, sleep is really just a luxury for people who don't have real responsibilities. My ex-husband used to sleep nine hours a night. Nine! Can you imagine? He was a graphic designer, if you can even call it that. Mostly he just sat around in sweatpants playing video games and complaining that I worked too much. I bought him this incredibly expensive espresso machine for our anniversary once—top of the line, imported from Switzerland—thinking maybe it would give him some drive. But he just used it to make these ridiculous caramel macchiatos that were basically just milk and sugar. Anyway, no, I don't get unusually energetic. I'm just driven. You have to be when everyone is waiting for you to fail.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies experiencing periods of being unusually energetic.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient denies needing much less sleep than usual, stating she sleeps fine once she is able to get to sleep.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? No. No, I don't really get sad like that. I mean, I don't have the time to just sit around moping. Though, if you want to talk about moping, you should see my executive assistant, Marcus. He came into my office last Tuesday looking absolutely miserable, going on and on about his seasonal allergies. Allergies! Can you believe that? I told him, Marcus, if you want to see real problems, try dealing with our vendors. 

We hired this catering company for the quarterly board meeting, and they were supposed to serve wild-caught salmon. I specifically requested it, it was in the contract. But I know for a fact it was farm-raised. You can tell by the color, it's this unnatural, almost neon pink, and the texture is just complete mush. I refused to pay the invoice. You can't just lie about salmon and expect me to sign a check. People think they can pull one over on me just because I'm a woman in charge, and they always try to serve that cheap farm-raised garbage. 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Something about being sad? No, no, I'm not depressed.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling depressed or sad, stating 'No, I don't really get sad like that' and 'I'm not depressed.'

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe you have any special powers, talents, or importance that other people don't have?
turns.patient_response:
Special powers? No, I don't... I mean, I'm just very good at what I do. I built this company from the ground up, so of course I have a certain level of importance, but it's not a superpower. It's just competence. Which is shockingly rare these days. 

Speaking of competence, you wouldn't believe the absolute disaster at the dry cleaners yesterday. I've been going to this place on 5th Avenue for three years—three years!—and I brought in my favorite silk blouse, the emerald green one I bought in Paris. It's vintage, completely irreplaceable. And the girl at the counter, she couldn't have been older than twenty, she just tossed it into this bin with all these heavy wool coats and denim jackets. I had to physically reach across the counter and rescue it. I told her, you can't just throw delicate silk in with rough fabrics, it causes friction, it ruins the weave! But she just looked at me with this completely blank expression, like I was speaking a foreign language. People just don't take pride in their work anymore. They just want to clock in, scroll on their phones, and collect a paycheck. It's exactly why I have to micromanage everything at the office. If I don't do it, who will? 

But, um... no, no magic powers or anything like that. Just common sense.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having any special powers, magic powers, or delusional importance, attributing her success to normal competence.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been hearing these voices?
turns.patient_response:
Well, the ones coming from the walls, or sometimes they come through my phone... that's been going on for about three months now. Three months. Which is exactly how long I've been trying to get the maintenance guy in my building to fix the HVAC unit in my condo. I swear, it's like pulling teeth with these people. I put in a work order in October. October! And every time I call the management office, it's the same runaround. "Oh, we're waiting on a part," or "Oh, the technician is out sick." It's just a constant stream of excuses. 

I actually went down to the lobby last week to confront the building manager, Susan. Susan is this incredibly mousy woman who always wears these terrible oversized cardigans that swallow her whole. I said to her, Susan, I pay six thousand dollars a month in HOA fees, the least you can do is ensure my condo is properly ventilated. And she had the nerve to tell me that I needed to fill out a secondary request form. A secondary form! As if the first one just magically vanished into thin air. It's just a complete lack of accountability. Nobody wants to take responsibility for anything anymore. They just want to pass the buck and hope you forget about it. But I don't forget. I document everything. 

But yeah, three months. About three months since I started hearing them.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly states they have been hearing voices coming from the walls and through their phone for about three months.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, unprompted, and highly detailed story about their building's maintenance and management in response to a simple question about the duration of their hallucinations.

turns.doctor_question: Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts are hard to follow or seem disorganized?
turns.patient_response:
Hard to follow? No. No, not at all. If anything, I'm the only one making any sense most of the time. I communicate very clearly—you absolutely have to when you're running a company. 

Though, if you want to talk about disorganized thoughts, you really should see the emails my marketing director, Chloe, sends out. It is absolute chaos. She doesn't use bullet points, she just writes these massive, rambling paragraphs, and last week she started using emojis in our internal memos. Emojis! I had to pull her into my office and explain that we are a serious firm, not a middle school group chat. 

And don't even get me started on her font choices. She used a purple script font for a Q3 projection report. Purple! I told her, Chloe, if I wanted to read a teenager's diary, I'd go buy one. It's just a complete lack of professionalism. It reminds me of my niece, actually. My sister just bought her this massive glitter gel pen set for her birthday, and now everything she writes is practically illegible. Which is fine when you're nine, but not when you're making six figures to manage a corporate brand. My sister completely spoils that kid, though. She bought her a miniature horse for Christmas last year. A literal horse. Who buys a horse when you live in a townhouse in the suburbs? Where do you even put it? The zoning laws alone must be a nightmare to navigate. 

Anyway... wait, what was the question? Did someone say my thoughts were hard to follow? No, nobody's ever told me that. I'm perfectly articulate.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient displays inflated self-confidence by claiming they are the only one making sense and insisting they are perfectly articulate.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient explicitly denies that their speech or thoughts are hard to follow or disorganized, despite their response being highly tangential.

turns.doctor_question: Have people told you that you go off track or give overly detailed answers when they ask you simple questions?
turns.patient_response:
Off track? Me? I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever said that to my face. I like to be thorough. If you ask a question, you should get the full picture. It's just like when I asked my contractor, Dave, about the timeline for the kitchen remodel. I asked a simple question: when will the cabinets be installed? And he gave me this vague, one-word answer. "Soon." What does "soon" even mean? In the construction world, "soon" could mean next Tuesday or it could mean 2026. 

And the worst part is, he's the one who insisted on custom Italian marble countertops, which took six months to ship. Six months! I had to live with a plywood island while we waited. And then, when the marble finally arrived, they scratched the hardwood floors bringing it in. I have Brazilian cherry floors, they are incredibly sensitive to moisture and scratching. I told him to put down a protective tarp, but did he listen? No. He just dragged this massive slab of rock right across the threshold. I had to hire a specialist from out of state just to buff out the gouges. The specialist was this lovely guy named Antonio, actually. He told me all about his family's vineyard back in Tuscany. They produce a really robust Chianti, which is my absolute favorite to pair with a good osso buco. I tried to make osso buco once, but finding quality veal shanks in this city is next to impossible unless you have an in with a private butcher. 

So, no, I don't go off track. I just think details matter. If people can't handle a complete answer, maybe they shouldn't ask the question.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient explicitly denies going off track or giving overly detailed answers, stating 'nobody's ever said that to my face' and 'no, I don't go off track' (despite demonstrating tangential speech in their response).

turns.doctor_question: Have you seen things that other people could not see?
turns.patient_response:
Seen things? Like, visions or something? No, I don't... I don't see things that aren't there. My eyesight is perfectly fine. I actually just had my annual exam with Dr. Lin. Dr. Lin is fantastic, by the way, his office is in that new medical plaza off 4th Street. The architecture there is stunning, all glass and steel, very mid-century modern. It reminds me of the corporate headquarters we almost leased back in 2019. 

We had this incredible broker, Marcus, who showed us this penthouse suite with panoramic views of the skyline. It was breathtaking. But the lease terms were absolutely draconian. They wanted a ten-year commitment with a six percent annual escalation clause. Six percent! I told Marcus, I said, Marcus, do I look like I just fell off the turnip truck? We ended up staying in our current building, which is fine, but the elevators are a nightmare. You press the button for the 14th floor and half the time it stops on 9 for no reason. Just stops. The doors open, nobody's there, and then it just sits there for a solid minute before it closes again. It's a complete waste of time. Time is money, and I don't have time to be trapped in a metal box on the 9th floor. The 9th floor is where the accounting firm is, anyway, and they always microwave fish in their breakroom. It seeps into the elevator shaft. Disgusting. 

But no, to answer your question, I haven't seen anything unusual. Just the usual incompetence everywhere I look.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits marked tangentiality, drifting from the topic of hallucinations to an eye exam, architecture, office leases, elevators, and microwaved fish.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies experiencing visual hallucinations, stating they do not see things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Has anyone ever told you that your speech is hard to follow because you jump from one topic to another?
turns.patient_response:
Jump from topic to topic? No, I don't think anyone's ever said that to me. People actually tell me I'm very focused. Hyper-focused, really. You have to be when you're managing a team of sixty people. 

Although, speaking of jumping around, you should see the new project management software IT just rolled out. It is a disaster. It's supposed to streamline our workflow, but it just bounces you from one tab to another, and nothing syncs properly. I was trying to approve a budget for the Q4 marketing push—the one Chloe is messing up with her emojis—and the system just froze. Completely locked up. I had to call Derek in IT, and he took forty-five minutes to reset my permissions. Forty-five minutes! And he was eating something crunchy on the phone the entire time. I think it was pita chips. Who eats pita chips while on a support call with the CEO? It's so disrespectful. 

I actually love pita chips, though, especially with a good roasted red pepper hummus. I used to make my own hummus from scratch. You have to soak the chickpeas overnight with a little baking soda, it makes the skins peel right off so the texture is perfectly smooth. My ex-husband hated it, he said it tasted too earthy, but he had the palate of a toddler. He practically lived on frozen chicken tenders. Which, honestly, explains a lot about why we got divorced. You can't build a life with a man who considers ketchup a vegetable. 

But anyway, no. I don't jump from topic to topic. I'm very direct.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient explicitly denies that anyone has told her she jumps from topic to topic and states she does not do so.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in being around other people?
turns.patient_response:
Less interested? I guess you could say that. I mean, I used to be the person driving every single idea, calling people after openings, organizing the networking dinners... I was relentless. Now, I can just sit at my desk for hours staring at the agenda. I barely speak to my husband or my staff, and I feel almost nothing about the work I used to love. 

But honestly, the agendas they give us now are printed on this terrible, glossy paper. It reflects the overhead lights right into your eyes. We used to use a nice, matte ivory stock, 32-pound weight. It had a real tactile quality to it, you know? When you handed someone an agenda printed on that paper, they knew you meant business. Our supplier was this local printing press down on 8th Avenue, run by this older couple, the Hendersons. Mr. Henderson always wore these fantastic vintage suspenders. He collected them, actually. He told me he had a pair that belonged to a railroad tycoon from the 1920s. 

Railroads are fascinating, really. The way they built this country. I took a train across the Canadian Rockies once, the Rocky Mountaineer. The glass-dome cars give you this incredible view of the mountains, but the coffee they served on board was just dreadful. It tasted like it had been sitting on a burner since Calgary. I don't understand why it's so hard to make a decent cup of coffee. You just need filtered water and freshly ground beans. It's not rocket science. My espresso machine at home has a built-in burr grinder, which is essential for the crema. 

But yeah, I just... I don't really care to be around anyone right now. I just sit there.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from agendas to paper quality, a printing press, suspenders, railroads, and finally coffee machines.
symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient describes a loss of motivation and social interest, stating they sit for hours, barely speak to their husband or staff, and feel 'almost nothing'.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly states they feel almost nothing about the work they used to love and do not care to be around anyone right now.

turns.doctor_question: Before the voices started, were you functioning better at work or in your relationships than you are now?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, absolutely. It's night and day. I mean, I’m just no longer reliably able to run the division right now, or even keep up with basic executive decisions. I've noticed the senior staff have quietly taken over the work I used to handle myself. Which is fine, I suppose, because Sarah—she's our VP of Operations—has always wanted more control anyway. She has this very aggressive management style. She read that book by the former Navy SEAL about extreme ownership and bought copies for the entire management team last Christmas. I thought it was a bit presumptuous. Books make terrible corporate gifts, honestly. One year, a vendor sent us these beautiful custom leather-bound notebooks instead. Italian leather. The smell was incredible. I love the smell of real leather, it reminds me of my grandfather's old Mercedes. He had this vintage SL, cherry red with a tan interior. We used to drive down to the coast on weekends and stop at this little seafood shack...

But, um, anyway. Yes, at home it's the same story. My husband has had to manage pretty much all the household responsibilities lately. I just leave things unfinished, or I don't start them at all. I tried to organize the pantry last week, pulled out all the canned goods, and then just left them sitting all over the kitchen island. They're probably still there. Speaking of canned goods, have you noticed how expensive imported tomatoes have gotten? San Marzano tomatoes used to be so reasonable, and now they're practically a luxury item. You really need them if you're making a proper marinara, though. The acidity is just completely different from domestic brands. If you use regular crushed tomatoes, you have to add a pinch of sugar to balance it out, which is just cheating in my opinion.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient states they are unable to keep up with work duties and leave household chores unfinished or unstarted.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes trying to organize the pantry but failing, leaving canned goods scattered across the kitchen.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits significant tangentiality and derailment, drifting from work to corporate gifts, leather, and cars, and later from organizing the pantry to the price of imported tomatoes.

turns.doctor_question: Over the last few months, have you felt emotionally flat or had trouble feeling much of anything?
turns.patient_response:
Emotionally flat? Yeah, I suppose so. Like I said before... I used to be the one driving every single idea, calling people after openings, just relentlessly pushing things forward. But now? I can just sit at my desk for hours, staring at the agenda. I barely speak to my husband or my staff. I just feel almost nothing about the work I used to absolutely love. 

It’s strange, though, because I used to have so much energy for it. I’d be up at 5 AM, answering emails, drinking that awful office coffee. We had this Keurig machine in the breakroom, and everyone always left the old pods in there. It drove me crazy. It’s not that hard to just pop it out and throw it away. People are so lazy when it comes to shared spaces. It’s like the tragedy of the commons, right? Everyone just assumes someone else will clean it up. We actually had to hire a day porter just to keep the kitchen from turning into a biohazard. His name was Luis, lovely guy, always humming to himself. He hummed a lot of Frank Sinatra. "Fly Me to the Moon," mostly. 

Sinatra had such a distinct voice. You don't really hear phrasing like that anymore in modern music. Everything now is so over-produced, so much auto-tune. It takes the soul right out of it. My husband listens to this electronic dance music when he works out, and it just sounds like a dial-up modem having a panic attack. I don't know how anyone finds a rhythm in that. I prefer classical for working out, honestly. Vivaldi’s Four Seasons is surprisingly good for cardio. The tempo in "Summer" really gets your heart rate up. 

But yeah, the feeling nothing part... that's exactly it. Just staring at the paper, feeling completely empty about all of it.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from work to coffee machines, a day porter, Frank Sinatra, and workout music before returning to the topic.
symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient describes emotional flatness, avolition (sitting at desk for hours staring), and asociality (barely speaking to husband or staff).
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly states feeling 'completely empty about all of it,' indicating emptiness and emotional numbness.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient reports feeling almost nothing about the work they used to 'absolutely love,' indicating a marked loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities.
